criterion: the gear Stan declares the three ZI data variables
why: Without them nothing else in this file can settle D6.

criterion: theta_C is declared ZERO-SIZE when zi_catch = 0
why: This is the whole basis of the OFF path being bit-identical rather than merely similar: a zero-size parameter consumes no element of the unconstrained vector and no initialization draw. G1 proves it empirically against the committed R5 render.

criterion: the season total is scaled by zi_scale, so turning ZI on cannot inflate it
why: lambda_C is fitted to the non-inflated component and rises to absorb the zeros theta_C removes, so an unscaled total would be inflated by 1/(1 - theta_C) purely by turning the feature on. The pooled model has done this since 2026-09-02.

criterion: every variable the gear Stan declares is built in prep_bss_crab_gear.R
why: The 2026-08-25 batch declared five variables that no prep built; Stan failed at data initialization on every fit, rstan returned an empty stanfit instead of raising, and every fit of every rung was lost to it. Missing: none

criterion: the SHIPPED config still fits the gear track without ZI
why: The D6 Stan port is inert until this key names this track. If it shipped as both, the next production gear render would silently change and the committed R5 cross-check figure quoted in PULL_REQUEST.md would go stale without anyone touching a number.

criterion: the SHIPPED gear all-gear period is still month
why: Same promise for D3: the lever is exposed, not moved.

criterion: the fit used the resolution the rung asked for
why: Read from ar_escalation_log.csv, which records what the sampler was actually given. A rung that fell back would otherwise report itself as the resolution it requested and sit in the ladder as a duplicate of another rung.

criterion: every fit in the rung passes the convergence gate
observed: 4 of 4 fits report BSS; gate all-pass = TRUE
why: Decision rule 1. A rung whose fits do not sample is not a candidate resolution, whatever its adequacy statistics say: the gate is the single authority on method selection and a PE fallback inside a rung makes its port total a different estimator from the other rungs'.

criterion: adequacy: p_loo is a small fraction of n_obs and few Pareto k are bad
observed: p_loo_frac 0.0368 (worst stream gear); 0 bad k of 1,651 obs (0.0%); PIT bias 0.0080; cov50 dev 0.0788; min disp n_eff 9,443
threshold: p_loo_frac <= 0.15 and bad k <= 5% of n_obs
why: Decision rule 2, calibrated on the pooled ladder: the daily fit that was rejected as overfitted sat at p_loo 0.352 with 41 bad k; the weekly fit that replaced it at 0.095 with 0; the gear R5 monthly fit at 0.0368 with 0. p_loo far above the number of parameters the model actually has is the signature of a latent process being fitted to individual observations.

criterion: REPORTED, NOT A CRITERION: the cross-track shore all-gear gap
why: Decision rule 5. Agreement between the two tracks at a COMMON resolution is a corroboration of the fishery model; choosing this track's resolution so as to minimize the gap would tune one estimate to another estimate instead of to the data, and would make the corroboration circular. It is printed so the reader can see the gap close, and excluded from the recommendation by construction.

criterion: THE D6 STAN EDIT IS INERT WHEN OFF: G1 is bit-identical to the pre-edit render
threshold: every shared parameter row identical to gear-type-CPUE-model-IMP-R5-gear-crosscheck-newf
why: G1 ships the same configuration as the committed R5 cross-check and differs from it only in carrying a Stan file with the ZI block compiled in but switched off. theta_C is declared vector[zi_catch], so at zi_catch = 0 it is zero-size and consumes neither a parameter nor an initialization draw. If this FAILS, the edit is not inert, the 93,274 R5 figure in PULL_REQUEST.md is no longer reproducible, and EVERY rung in this ladder is measuring the edit as well as its own lever.

criterion: the port total reproduces the committed R5 figure
why: A weaker restatement of the row above, in the unit a reader will quote.

criterion: D6 rule 2: the paired elpd gain exceeds 2 paired SE
observed: NA nats at NA paired SE (NA SE)
why: Paired, not naive: on the pooled Z1/Z0 pair the paired SE was 5.5 nats against a naive 46.7, which is the difference between 2.69 SE and 0.32 SE. The pooled adoption earned +11.6 nats at 2.30 SE.

criterion: D6 rule 4: the gain is not bought entirely at the zeros
threshold: the positive-count loss is smaller than the zero-count gain
why: A zero-inflation parameter that earns its elpd purely at the zeros while degrading the positive counts is doing something different from one that improves the fit everywhere, and the aggregate number cannot tell them apart. On the pooled pair the split was +25.2 at the zeros and -10.5 at the positives: net positive, but bought.

criterion: D6 rule 3: both count bins improve
why: The pooled adoption halved both (zero +3.7 -> +2.0, one -6.1 -> -3.3). A feature that fixes the zero bin by breaking the one bin is moving the misfit, not removing it, which is what an earlier reading of the prototype got wrong and had to retract.

criterion: theta_C is identified and not pinned at its prior
why: A theta_C sitting on its prior mean means the data did not inform it and the elpd gain, if any, came from somewhere else. kappa_OSP is the standing example of a parameter whose reported median is its prior.

criterion: REPORTED, NOT A CRITERION: the port total under ZI
why: The season total is multiplied by (1 - theta_C) in generated quantities precisely so that turning the feature on does not inflate it. A total that barely moves is the design working, not weak evidence, and a total that moves a lot would be the thing to investigate.
